Macro or AI-spending slowdown: Datadog's consumption model means revenue can shrink quickly if enterprise workloads contract. Palo Alto competitive pressure: Palo Alto acquired Chronosphere for $3.35B in January 2026 and told analysts it can deliver comparable observability at one-third the cost; BofA flagged pricing compression risk for Datadog and peers. The Avadel LUMRYZ settlement (October 2025) resolved litigation, but the underlying sodium oxybate patent landscape remains a long-term structural risk to the sleep portfolio. Acquisition integration and milestone risk: Actio deal closes in late 2026 or 2027; $500 million of the price is contingent on development and regulatory success. Profitability cliff: Trailing net income is $20 million annualized on near-$5 billion equity; the company is only nominally profitable despite $5+ billion debt, and oncology expansion requires sustained investment spending. FX and one-time items: Q2 guidance raise noted that prior-year growth was boosted by one-time pricing adjustments and FX tailwinds in ex-U.S. markets, which management expects to normalize in coming quarters, making future growth appear slower than headline comparisons.
